newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA's Fraser sees solid growth, low inflation.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA's Fraser sees solid growth, low inflation.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Bernie Fraser said that solid growth and low inflation were set to continue for some time and that he saw no threats on the horizon to extending the six year run of uniterrupted growth.
"Solid growth and low inflation are set to continue in Australia for some time yet," Fraser said in a speech at a BZW seminar in Tokyo. A copy of the speech was released in Sydney.

"Our domestic forecasts suggest that 1996/97 will be a year of reasonable growth in Australia, with inflation comfortably within the 2-3 per cent target and the current account deficit relatively subdued," Fraser said.
Fraser said Australia was now into its sixth year of uninterrupted economic growth, "and this phase is set to continue for some time yet."

Fraser said interruptions to growth in Australia were usually the result of a slowdown in world growth, or a severe shock to the domestic economy such as a surge in spending or a blowout in wages which threatened to bring on inflation or current account problems.
"No such threats are on the horizon at this time," he said.
While some Asian economies were coming off the boil, the indicators for most countries, particularly the U.S., "are reasonably encouraging," Fraser said.
The government has forecast gross domestic product to grow 3.5 percent in year average terms the 1996/97 year ending June 30, from 4.1 percent in 1995/96.
